sn6.11:1.3: Sanaṅkumāra (“Everyoung”) became a Hindu deity closely associated with the worship of Krishna. He first appears in the seventh chapter of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad. He speaks this verse also at [dn3:1.28.2](), [dn27:32.2](), [mn53:25.3](), [an11.10:6.1](), and it was endorsed by the Buddha. His appearance is heralded by a great light in the north, and he features in two extended discussions among the gods ([dn18:15.1](), [dn19:15.1]()).
